subject: Status - US state model reproduced, the template is harder than it looks
body:
Status through Apr 15.

Reproduction: done, state level. Our numbers track the published evaluation notebook within ~3% on the 14-day horizon. The Japan prefecture model we skipped deliberately - different constructor, no value for us.

The Apr 24 milestone is the one at risk. "Strip out the COVID-specific parts and leave a reusable template" sounded clean in the kickoff, but the compartmental structure isn't a plug-in - the encoders are wired to specific rate parameters, and the shared helper functions in the base definitions assume epidemiological features (population density, mobility). For a queue-depth forecast there is no analogue of an infection rate, so you're not reusing the model, you're reusing a design pattern plus about 200 lines.

My recommendation: retarget Apr 24 to a written design pattern + a worked port, and stop pretending we're shipping a framework. Maren agrees. It's less impressive and more true.

Halima
